learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and structure of an ExecutionList (ExecutionFolder → ExecutionList → ExecutionEntry).
Create an ExecutionList Folder and an ExecutionList, then populate it with TestCases via drag-and-drop.
Distinguish ExecutionLists (store historic results) from the ScratchBook (temporary results only).
Understand that a TestCase can be used an unlimited number of times in the same ExecutionList.
Execute tests from an ExecutionList and interpret the results (Passed / Failed / Not Executed) via the ActualLog.

elements.description: A structured list in the Execution section of Tosca Commander that runs TestCases and stores their results. Its key job is to execute TestCases AND keep a permanent record of every result.
The Execution section is organized in three levels:
items: ExecutionFolder — a container that groups ExecutionLists (e.g., 'Exercise 21 - Create an ExecutionList').
ExecutionList — the actual runnable list (e.g., 'Web Shop'). This is what you Run.
ExecutionEntry — a single TestCase placed inside an ExecutionList. Dragging a TestCase in creates an ExecutionEntry.
ActualLog — the result record created inside the ExecutionList after a run, timestamped (e.g., 'created: 8/11/2021 11:28 AM').

elements.term: ExecutionList vs. ScratchBook — results persistence (confirmed exam point)
elements.description: The defining difference is what happens to the results:
items: ExecutionList — stores ALL historic results permanently (via the ActualLog). You can consult past runs any time.
ScratchBook — results are TEMPORARY. Each new run overwrites the previous one; nothing is kept.
Use the ScratchBook for quick trial/debug runs; use an ExecutionList for formal, recorded execution.

elements.description: The same TestCase can be added to an ExecutionList an UNLIMITED number of times. Each entry runs independently — enabling the same test to run with different data sets or configurations.

elements.text: An ExecutionList is like a playlist: select your songs (TestCases), arrange them in order, and hit play. The same song can appear multiple times in the playlist, and each play is independent.

elements.caption: ExecutionList runs TestCases top-to-bottom. Same TestCase can appear unlimited times. Results: Passed / Failed / Not Executed.

bulletPoints: ExecutionLists live in the ExecutionLists section — separate from TestCases, Modules, Requirements.
TestCase reuse limit: UNLIMITED — confirmed AS1 exam question.
ScratchBook = built-in ad-hoc list for quick runs. No setup needed.

elements.title: Setting up and running an ExecutionList (Exercise 21 procedure):
items: Prerequisite: confirm the TestCases are COMPLETED and all Business Parameters are entered.
In the Execution section, under Execution >> ExecutionLists, create an ExecutionList Folder (e.g., 'Exercise 21').
Inside that folder, create a new ExecutionList and name it (e.g., 'Web Shop').
Select the COMPLETED TestCases and drag them ONTO the ExecutionList 'Web Shop' — they become ExecutionEntries.
Click Run in the ExecutionLists ribbon (or right-click the ExecutionList → Run) to execute all entries sequentially.
Review results in the ActualLog: Passed (green) / Failed (red) / Not Executed. Save your work.

elements.text: Drop target matters: drop TestCases ONTO the ExecutionList (green flag) to add them as ExecutionEntries. If you drop them onto an ExecutionFolder instead, Tosca creates a SEPARATE new ExecutionList for each TestCase (named <New ExecutionList>, <New ExecutionList>_1, ...).

elements.title: Reading execution results:
items: Passed — green indicator; all TestSteps completed successfully
Failed — red indicator; click the entry to see which specific step failed and the error message
Not Executed — the TestCase was skipped (e.g., a preceding test failed and blocked it)

bulletPoints: Tests execute top-to-bottom in the order they appear in the ExecutionList.
Click a failed entry to see the exact failed step and error detail.

examPitfalls.title: TestCase reuse limit — Unlimited, not Once or Twice
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam asks: 'How often can you use a TestCase in the same ExecutionList?' Distractors: 'Once', 'Twice', 'Set in TestCase properties'.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The correct answer is UNLIMITED. A TestCase can appear any number of times in the same ExecutionList. This is a confirmed AS1 exam question.

examPitfalls.title: ExecutionList stores historic results; ScratchBook does not
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which option keeps a permanent record of test results, or how ExecutionLists differ from the ScratchBook. Candidates think both behave the same.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ExecutionLists STORE all historic results permanently (in the ActualLog) — you can consult past runs any time. ScratchBook results are TEMPORARY and overwritten on the next run. Use ScratchBook for quick trials, ExecutionLists for recorded execution.

examPitfalls.title: Drag-drop target — ExecutionList vs. ExecutionFolder
examPitfalls.trapDescription: When adding several TestCases, dropping them onto an ExecutionFolder creates a SEPARATE new ExecutionList per TestCase (<New ExecutionList>, _1, _2) instead of one list with multiple entries.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Drop the TestCases directly ONTO the ExecutionList (green flag) to add them as ExecutionEntries in one list. Dropping onto the ExecutionFolder creates one new list per TestCase.

examPitfalls.title: TestCases should be COMPLETED before adding to an ExecutionList
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates add unfinished TestCases and forget to enter Business Parameters, causing runtime failures.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Before adding TestCases to an ExecutionList, confirm their WorkState is COMPLETED and that all Business Parameters are filled in. Exercise 21 adds only the COMPLETED TestCases (exercises 13, 15, 20).

examPitfalls.title: ExecutionList vs. TestCase section
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where ExecutionLists are found. Candidates confuse their location with the TestCases section.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ExecutionLists have their own dedicated Execution section in Tosca Commander — separate from TestCases, Modules, and Requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How often can the same TestCase be used within a single ExecutionList?

options.text: Unlimited — the same TestCase can be added any number of times.
Once — duplicate entries are automatically removed.
Twice — a maximum of two entries per TestCase per ExecutionList.
The limit is set in the TestCase properties tab.

practiceQuiz.hint: No limit — confirmed directly in the official knowledge check.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestCase can be used an unlimited number of times in the same ExecutionList. Each entry is an independent execution. This is confirmed as a direct AS1 exam question.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to quickly run a single TestCase without setting up a formal ExecutionList. What built-in feature of Tosca Commander should they use?

options.text: The Debug Console.
The ScratchBook.
The TestCase Viewer.
A temporary ExecutionList that auto-deletes after execution.

practiceQuiz.hint: It is a pre-existing, built-in ad-hoc execution area.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The ScratchBook is Tosca's built-in ad-hoc ExecutionList. It exists specifically for quick, informal test runs without the overhead of creating and naming a formal ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In which section of Tosca Commander are ExecutionLists found?

options.text: In the TestCases section, as a sub-folder of the test hierarchy.
In the Modules section, alongside module definitions.
In their own dedicated ExecutionLists section, separate from TestCases and Modules.
In the Requirements section, linked to requirement coverage.

practiceQuiz.hint: Each major area in Tosca has its own section.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionLists have their own dedicated section in Tosca Commander — separate from TestCases, Modules, and Requirements. This mirrors the four-section structure of Tosca Commander.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester needs a permanent, historic record of every test run that can be consulted weeks later. Which Tosca feature keeps this record?

options.text: The ScratchBook — it archives every run automatically.
The Modules section.
The TestCase WorkState field.
An ExecutionList — it stores all historic results in the ActualLog.

practiceQuiz.hint: Historic results = one specific execution feature.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ExecutionLists store all historic results permanently in the ActualLog, so past runs can be consulted any time. The ScratchBook only keeps a temporary result that is overwritten on the next run.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester selects three TestCases and drags them onto the ExecutionFolder. Tosca creates '<New ExecutionList>', '<New ExecutionList>_1', and '<New ExecutionList>_2', each with one TestCase — but the tester wanted ONE list with three entries. What went wrong?

options.text: They dropped onto the ExecutionFolder instead of onto an ExecutionList — dropping on a folder creates a new list per TestCase.
The TestCases were not COMPLETED, so Tosca split them.
Tosca always creates one ExecutionList per TestCase; this is expected.
The Business Parameters were missing.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Dropping TestCases onto an ExecutionFolder makes Tosca create a separate new ExecutionList for each one. To get one list with three ExecutionEntries, first create the ExecutionList, then drop the TestCases directly ONTO that ExecutionList (the green-flag node).

quickRecap.value: Ordered list of TestCases to execute. Lives in its own section in Tosca Commander.
UNLIMITED — the same TestCase can appear any number of times in one ExecutionList.
ExecutionList STORES historic results (ActualLog). ScratchBook results are TEMPORARY — overwritten each run.
ExecutionFolder (container) → ExecutionList (runnable) → ExecutionEntry (a TestCase). ActualLog = result record.
Drop TestCases ONTO the ExecutionList (green flag) = entries in one list. Onto the folder = a new list per TestCase.
Entries run top-to-bottom. Run via the ExecutionLists ribbon 'Run' button (not F6 — that's ScratchBook).
Passed (green) / Failed (red) / Not Executed. Failure shows the specific step and error.
